title: Empanadas de Manzana con Queso
description: A twist on traditional empanadas, these Argentine-inspired pastries are filled with caramelized apples and melted cheese, perfect for a cozy autumn evening.

ingredients.name: Empanada dough (homemade or store-bought, gluten-free)
ingredients.notes: Make sure to use a gluten-free empanada dough to accommodate dietary restrictions.

ingredients.name: Apples, peeled and sliced
ingredients.notes: A mix of sweet and tart apples, such as Granny Smith and Gala, works well for this recipe.

ingredients.name: Onion, chopped
ingredients.notes: Caramelize the onion to bring out its natural sweetness.

ingredients.name: Garlic, minced
ingredients.notes: Add a punch of flavor with roasted garlic.

ingredients.name: Grated cheese (Monterey Jack or Cheddar work well)
ingredients.notes: The cheese will melt and add creaminess to the filling.

ingredients.name: Egg, beaten (for egg wash)
ingredients.notes: Use the beaten egg to brush the empanadas before baking for a golden glaze.

ingredients.name: Salt and pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the filling and dough as needed to bring out the flavors.

instructions: Roll out the empanada dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
In a pan, caramelize the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the sliced apples to the pan and cook until tender.
Mix in the grated cheese and season with salt and pepper.
Place a tablespoon of the apple-cheese mixture onto one half of each dough circle.
Brush the edges with the beaten egg and fold the other half of the dough over the filling.
Press the edges to seal the empanada and use a fork to crimp.
Brush the tops with the remaining egg wash and cut a few slits for steam to escape.
Bake the empanadas for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
